group: Reported fixes: defects found in use, and the tests that guard them

name: A program update locked every existing tenant out
sub: Your comment 2026-10-03 (discuss): find a break early. Answered as ask 2
decided: Yes (check every still-served version's ops against the new schema; refuse a break unless the developer confirms).
explain:
What you saw: after a restart, signing in to your tenant answered that its database could not be reached.

  • Cause: a program update reached the deployment's own database and no tenant's. Your tenant stayed one version behind and was held closed.
  • Wrong message: it blamed an unreachable database; the real reason was only in /health/ready.
  • Why it matters: with one tenant per person, every update would lock out every person.

Watch for a regression if: a tenant is held closed after an apply, or /health/ready lists a tenant as schema behind.

Guarding tests: crates/ordo-host/tests/tenant_forward.rs (six: two tenants and an additive change, a direct apply caught up, a sweep with no request, a database down during the apply, a refused change, a dropped field); two in notes_app.rs (people keep working across a field added then removed; a refused tenant is closed alone with the new sentence); the refused case in apply_everywhere.rs.

asks.text: A new version now goes live once the deployment's own database takes it; a tenant that cannot follow is closed alone. Keep that?
asks.suggest: Keep it. The plan waited for every database, so one offline person would have blocked every update for everyone.

asks.text: When a new version is planned, should every still-served version's ops be checked against the new schema, refusing a break unless the developer confirms?
asks.suggest: Yes, as a pre-check. It finds a break before any tenant is affected. Backward-compatible changes, like additions, pass without a prompt, which is the design discipline you described.

where: crates/ordo-host/src/schema_apply.rs (bring_forward), tenant_forward.rs (CatchUp), apply_op.rs; ORDO_TENANT_CATCHUP_SECS. Checklist 25i.

name: The server stopped answering after a share was opened twice
sub: Reported 2026-09-29 by you. Fixed the same day
explain:
What you saw: passkey prompts stopped appearing; the server answered nothing, not even its health check.

  • Cause: two overlapping share lookups each waited on a single-connection store by blocking a server thread, while the answer needed that same part of the server.
  • Fix: every such store tells the server it is about to wait (ordo_exec::bridge).

Watch for a regression if: the server holds its port but answers nothing, with every thread idle.

Guarding tests in crates/ordo-host/tests/notes_app.rs: concurrent_share_peeks_never_stop_the_door_accepting, sigterm_with_a_live_feed_open_ends_the_process_within_its_grace, the_door_keeps_answering_through_sign_ups_a_share_and_an_accept_with_a_feed_open.
where: Merge ea00791: crates/ordo-exec/src/bridge.rs and every sync store bridge. Checklist 25f.

name: Each tenant held seven database connections for good
sub: Found 2026-09-29 while fixing the stopped server. Fixed the same day
explain:
What would have happened: a default Postgres ran out after about 12 sign-ups, and sign-ups then failed with too many clients.

  • Cause: every tenant's pool opened all its connections at once and kept them, plus a listener each.
  • Fix: connections open when needed and close when idle (ORDO_PG_IDLE_SECS, default 30); a tenant is listened to only while a live feed is open.

Watch for a regression if: connections in pg_stat_activity grow with the number of tenants rather than with use.

Guarding tests: thirty_people_sign_up_on_a_default_server and an_idle_tenant_releases_its_connections_within_the_idle_period in crates/ordo-host/tests/notes_app.rs; crates/ordo-exec/tests/pool_idle.rs.
where: Merge 9ee955a: crates/ordo-exec/src/lib.rs (pool), crates/ordo-host/src/invalidation.rs. Checklist 25g.

name: New tenants were unreachable where the database needs a password
sub: Found 2026-09-29 by CI. You asked whether these failures could be product bugs; this one was
explain:
What CI saw: every sign-up's new tenant never came up; the notes app tests waited 10 seconds and failed.

  • Cause: the server dialled a tenant on its own Postgres with only the credentials file, not the password it already holds. The live deployment needs a password, so every sign-up there would have failed.
  • Fix: a tenant on the deployment's own cluster uses the deployment's own password; a separate file is only needed for another cluster.

Watch for a regression if: a new tenant never serves, or the log shows a tenant's members could not be read with an authentication error.

Guarding tests: the notes app tests in crates/ordo-host/tests/notes_app.rs run against a password database on CI; the_deployment_label_answers_with_the_deployments_own_password in crates/ordo-exec/tests/route.rs. Run them locally the CI way with the recipe in .claude/skills/testing/SKILL.md.
where: crates/ordo-exec/src/route.rs (WithOwnCredential), crates/ordo-host/src/runtime.rs, crates/ordo-cli/src/operator.rs; docs/deploying.md 4d.

name: The device filters some lists differently from the server
sub: Found 2026-09-29, fixed 2026-09-30. Two more fixes on the device: text normalization and the sort tiebreak
explain:
What would happen: a filtered list can come out differently offline than online.

  • Empty values: the device said null != 5 and null == null are false; Ordo says both are true.
  • Text order: the device orders by 16-bit units, the server by bytes. They differ on rarer characters such as emoji.

Where: clients/ordo-sdk/src/replica/refine.ts, the ne case and compare.

Watch for a regression if: a list filtered on the device shows different rows or order than the same read online.

Guarding tests: one shared case table, crates/ordo-conformance/fixtures/refine-parity.json (57 cases), run on the device by clients/ordo-sdk/test/refine-parity.test.ts and through the real server read path by crates/ordo-conformance/tests/refine_parity.rs. Both read the same file, so the device and the server cannot drift apart unnoticed.
where: clients/ordo-sdk/src/replica/refine.ts. Checklist 25k, 25l.

name: The server answered two kinds of filter against the language's rules
sub: Found 2026-09-30 by the parity test. Fixed the same day
explain:
What would have happened: some filters answered differently from what the language promises, on every deployment.

  • Text order in filters: < and > on text followed the database's locale, so the answer depended on how Postgres was installed. Only sorting followed Ordo's rule.
  • in with an empty value: it never matched a row whose value was empty, though the language says it should.

Guarding tests: one shared case table, crates/ordo-conformance/fixtures/refine-parity.json (57 cases), run on the device by clients/ordo-sdk/test/refine-parity.test.ts and through the real server read path by crates/ordo-conformance/tests/refine_parity.rs. Both read the same file, so the device and the server cannot drift apart unnoticed.

Watch for a regression if: the same filter answers differently on two deployments, or a filter with in misses rows with empty values.
where: crates/ordo-plan/src/lib.rs (COLLATE "C" on text comparisons; in with a null member). Checklist 25m, 25n.

name: Custody records lost the name of the command that made them
explain:
Five operator commands wrote their security record with no command name.

  • Seen: ordo keys init, rotate, reseal, destroy and restore --record stored their op as <unprintable>.
  • Cause: the op had spaces; the recorder keeps only [A-Za-z0-9._-].
  • Fix: dotted names, ordo.keys.init and so on.
  • Regression looks like: <unprintable> as a custody record's op.
where: crates/ordo-cli/src/keys.rs, crates/ordo-exec/src/undo.rs; test every_custody_op_is_recorded_as_named in crates/ordo-cli/tests/custody_ops.rs

name: ordo dev wipes tables that are not its own
decided: Yeah - if things exist that aren't in schema don't wipe whats not yours. Just make a note of it - sinsible.
explain:
Seen: pointed at a shared database with ORDO_PG_HOST, the dev loop's reset runs DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE. It also resets on the first save when none of the program's tables exist yet.

Cause: dev_db::reset (crates/ordo-cli/src/dev_db.rs:442) drops the whole schema; classify never checks whose tables are there.

Fix: drop only the program's own tables. List anything else as present, not Ordo's. Your words (g24): if things exist that aren't in schema don't wipe whats not yours. Just make a note of it.

A regression looks like: a table the program never declared is gone after a dev reset.

Tests: owed with the fix.
where: crates/ordo-cli/src/dev_db.rs (reset, classify_tables), commit b65e205; tests dev_db::tests::classify_tables_sorts_by_ownership, a_foreign_table_survives_a_reset_and_ordos_own_are_reset

name: A ruling on one ask hid the whole task from Needs me
sub: Found 2026-10-03: public-data's 5 open asks vanished from Needs me. Fixed the same day
explain:
Seen: after rulings on asks 18 and 19 of public-data were recorded from conversation, the board said nothing needed you, though asks 15, 16, 17, 20 and 21 were open.

Cause: board.py record --ask N also wrote the task's decided field, and a task with decided set counts as settled whatever its asks say.

Fix: record writes decided only for a ruling on the task as a whole (no --ask). public-data's field was cleared; no other task had an open ask hidden.

A regression looks like: a task with an unanswered ask missing from Needs me right after a ruling on a different ask.

Tests: none; board.py has no test suite.
where: scripts/board.py cmd_record; data fix on public-data.

name: ordo check exits 0 when an op does not compile
explain:
A broken program passes any script that trusts ordo check's exit code.

  • Seen: it prints DOES NOT COMPILE for an op and exits 0.
  • Found: writing examples/syntax/, 2026-10-03.
  • Regression looks like: exit 0 beside a DOES NOT COMPILE line.

asks.text: Should ordo check exit non-zero when any op does not compile?
asks.suggest: Yes, exit 1. A check that passes a broken program is worse than none. market.ordo's giftOrders would need fixing or marking as expected to fail.

where: crates/ordo-cli/src/main.rs (check_exit, --expect-fail), crates/ordo-cli/src/lib.rs (uncompiled_ops); CI smoke steps in images.yml and release.yml; tests a_program_with_an_op_that_does_not_compile_exits_1, an_expected_failure_passes_and_a_stale_one_fails, a_program_that_compiles_exits_0 in crates/ordo-cli/tests/check_exit.rs

name: Undoing a board's create failed on its own access row
explain:
Any create on an entity with an acl could not be undone.

  • Seen: the undo was refused as access_guard.
  • Cause: it deleted the creator's admin access row first, then lost the right to delete the board.
  • Fix: every planned delete is checked before any runs.
  • Regression looks like: undoing an acl root's create refused.
where: crates/ordo-exec/src/undo.rs (judge_deletes), commit 2964fad; test reverting_a_board_create_takes_its_cards_and_access_rows in crates/ordo-exec/tests/owned_delete_revert.rs

name: A sealed field read through a join loses its seal
explain:
A sealed field read through a join was treated as plain text.

  • Seen: served 200 with the stored envelope as hex; no plaintext, no key release, no security event.
  • Cause: the join never set the list of fields to open; let and append had the same hole.
  • Fix: all three carry the seal; mismatched append arms are refused.
  • Regression looks like: such an output classed sql, or text starting \x.
where: crates/ordo-sema/src/lib.rs (bind_multi_source, let_source, append), commits 67b8626, 2056893; tests crates/ordo-conformance/tests/sealed_through_join.rs (8), crates/ordo-exec/tests/sealed_through_join.rs (the_executor_never_serves_a_joined_envelope_as_text)

name: A join cannot project fields from a filtered or guarded second source
explain:
Any join whose second source has a filter or a guard can project nothing from it.

  • Seen: customers[name] orders(status == "done")[placed] fails with projection_unknown_field.
  • Cause: that term's subquery returns only its join key.
  • Fix owed: project its fields, carrying sealed-ness with them.
where: crates/ordo-sema/src/lib.rs (filtered term sub-select), commit bf85ad4; tests crates/ordo-conformance/tests/join_filtered_term.rs (5)

name: The production door never ran the token gate
explain:
A withdrawn delegation or a dead share grant still got through the production door.

  • Seen: nothing; the Fable audit found it reading code.
  • Cause: the production access checker never forwarded the token gate, so it always passed.
  • Fix: it forwards the gate.
  • Regression looks like: a revoked delegation not refused as delegation_required.
where: crates/ordo-host/src/runtime.rs (SwappableAccess forwards token_gate, token_known), commit 801c48d; test the_swappable_door_forwards_the_token_gate in crates/ordo-host/tests/delegation.rs

name: Shutting down the security drain could lose events in flight
explain:
A graceful shutdown could drop security events the drain had taken but not written.

  • Seen: attached_tenant.rs failed under load.
  • Cause: shutdown aborted the drain mid-pass.
  • Fix: shutdown waits for the pass, then flushes.
  • Regression looks like: events missing after shutdown.
where: crates/ordo-host/src/secdrain.rs (shutdown joins the pass), commit fbf9acc; test crates/ordo-host/tests/secdrain_shutdown.rs

name: A filtered join term over-reports what an op reaches
explain:
An op built on a filtered join claims to read more than it does.

  • Seen: a composed op reaches a sealed field and does host work on paper, while it opens nothing.
  • Cause: the filtered term's sub-select carries every field and is never trimmed.
  • Direction: over-claims, never under-claims.
where: crates/ordo-sema/src/prune.rs, commit be6a10d; tests join_filtered_term::an_op_over_a_filtered_term_reaches_only_what_it_reads, a_filtered_term_used_only_in_a_filter_or_sort_keeps_those_columns

name: An open field cannot be indexed on its own
explain:
There is no way to write an index on one open field.

  • Seen: index (status) is refused and points to status: text index, which does not parse.
  • Matters because the cost guide's fix for a slow filter is to index the field.
  • Fix owed: the index field modifier, as the message promises.
where: crates/ordo-syntax/src/declparse.rs, crates/ordo-schema/src/lib.rs, commit ac22ff6; tests graph.rs::a_field_modifier_index_is_a_single_column_index, schema_apply.rs::a_field_modifier_index_is_added_to_an_existing_table

name: Four refinement values reached Postgres as a 500
explain:
A hostile sweep found four refinement values that crashed into a 500.

  • Seen: an impossible date, a NUL in text, a repeated pick, a too-long number.
  • Fix: each is invalid_refinement at the door; parameters had the same holes.
  • Regression looks like: any 500 from the audit sweep.
where: crates/ordo-api/src/bind.rs, refine.rs, commit 3e5b4db; tests crates/ordo-host/tests/refine_audit.rs, crates/ordo-api/tests/api.rs

name: Ref fields are not indexed, though the reference says they are
explain:
A filter on a ref field scans the whole table.

  • Seen: the reference marks auto-indexing of refs as settled; the DDL never creates the index.
  • Fix owed: one index per ref field, added to existing tables by the diff.
where: crates/ordo-schema (Entity::all_indexes), commit dafbb56; tests ref_fields_index_automatically, a_ref_added_to_an_existing_table_gets_its_index

name: A saturated connection pool answers 500
explain:
When the server is busy, callers are told it broke.

  • Seen: 500 internal: pool saturated, under load.
  • Ruled long ago: a saturated pool is a typed failure callers can retry.
  • Fix: a typed 503.
where: New class server_busy (503, Retry-After), commit 08ea743; tests server_busy_is_a_retryable_503_with_retry_after, a_full_pool_answers_server_busy_and_the_retry_lands

name: The production server never records a key release
explain:
A deployed server decrypts without counting or recording it.

  • Seen: only tests wrap the key provider in the layer that meters and records releases.
  • Matters: who decrypted what, and the alert on unusual releases, rest on it.
  • Fix: wrap it in the binary.
where: crates/ordo-host/src/runtime.rs (meter_custody), commit 12aef13; tests a_served_sealed_write_and_read_are_counted_and_recorded, the_reseal_worker_releases_through_the_metered_custody, every_holder_shares_one_custody_wrapped_once in crates/ordo-host/tests/key_release_metered.rs

name: Deleting an account left the person's delegations and recovery approvals
explain:
Found by the audit of 27aq; fixed the same day.

  • Account delete removed tables by their principal column only
  • $delegation and $recoveryapproval name a person in other columns, so their rows stayed
  • Fixed: each table lists every column that names a person, and a listed column a table lacks is an error
where: commit a406073 (crates/ordo-host/src/identity_removal.rs). Test crates/ordo-host/tests/member_release.rs: deleting_an_account_removes_its_delegations_and_recovery_approvals. Regression: a $delegation row naming the deleted id as delegator or agent, or a $recoveryapproval row naming it as approver, after the route answers 200. Audit: docs/audit-2026-10-05d.md finding 1.

name: The deployment's record of a bucket change lost who asked
explain:
Found by the audit of 2026-10-06; fixed the same day.

Since bucket changes moved to the deployment's stream, the record named the platform. It names the member again.
where: commit 03887a8c: BucketOps::record_change uses Subject::member. Test the_deployments_record_of_a_bucket_change_names_the_member_who_asked (crates/ordo-host/tests/attach_bucket.rs). Regression: subject system:attach-bucket. docs/audit-2026-10-06.md finding 3.

name: Twelve refusal classes decoded as internal in both clients
explain:
Found writing the sign-in guide; fixed the same day.

  • Each TypeScript client keeps its own list of refusal classes
  • 12 were missing, so a paused tenant read as an internal fault
  • Both lists now name all 61, and a test fails when one falls behind
where: commit c82154c0: clients/ordo-sdk/src/core/refusal.ts, clients/ordo-react/src/refusal.ts. Test crates/ordo-api/tests/client_classes.rs every_client_names_every_refusal_class_the_door_sends. Regression: a new ErrorCode with no client entry fails that test; in use, a known class arriving as internal.

name: Revoking one share wiped other live data from the device
explain:
Found by CI on 2026-10-08, from the React gaps fix; fixed the same day.

  • A revoked share poisoned the whole device copy at once
  • That wiped rows another live synced op still held
  • Now the copy is poisoned only when no synced op is still live; one op's release removes only its own rows
where: commit 6f6d83b9 (clients/ordo-react/src/device.ts onView), ordo-react 0.2.1. Test clients/ordo-react/test/device.test.ts 'a row another synced op still holds survives the revocation of this one' (50 runs clean). Regression: that test failing intermittently, or a still-shared note vanishing from the device when another share is closed.

name: The package workflow could publish from any branch when run by hand
explain:
Found by the audit of 2026-10-08; fixed the same day.

A manual run published from whatever branch it named. It now runs only on main in HominemAI.
where: commit 52e888e6 (.github/workflows/packages.yml). No test (a workflow condition). Regression: a manual run on another branch publishing. docs/audit-2026-10-08.md finding 3.

name: A tenant unreachable at boot replayed its whole history to routines
explain:
Found by the audit of 2026-10-08; fixed the same day.

A tenant first reached after boot started its routine cursor at 0, so routines acted on every past change. It now starts at the chain head, unless the tenant is newer than the deployed version.
where: commit 2075b038 (Tenants::register_on_reach, ordo_exec::registry::activated_at). Test crates/ordo-host/tests/routines.rs a_tenant_unreachable_at_boot_does_not_replay_its_history_when_reached. Regression: a routine acting on changes made before it was deployed. Also 321fa032: idle tenants backed off to ORDO_TRIGGERS_IDLE_MAX_SECS (10 s), stale cursors retired once caught up. docs/audit-2026-10-08.md findings 7 and 8.

name: An edit to only a routine was silently dropped on deploy
explain:
Found while building routine each bodies; fixed the same day.

Routines were not part of the program's version hash, so a change to only a routine kept the old version, and the deploy answered already stored and kept the old routine. Routines are now in the hash.
where: commit 45ed6647 (crates/ordo-plan/src/artifact.rs program_artifact gains routines). Test crates/ordo-cli/tests/schema_identity.rs a_change_to_only_a_routine_changes_the_programs_version. Regression: a routine-only edit applied with no new version. A program with no routines keeps its exact old version.

name: A blind-index lookup that returns a sealed field does not compile
explain: Seen (audit-2026-10-09 finding 1): op byEmail($e: text) = customers(email == $e)[name, email] fails ordo check, plan and apply with unresolved_blind_index. Cause: crates/ordo-plan/src/artifact.rs:620 skips planning only when the cost class is BlindIndex. The executor serves the same call. Regression: a declared blind-index read stops compiling.
where: crates/ordo-plan/src/artifact.rs (withholds the statement whenever the query holds a digest; cost::query_has_blind), commit ad3aaaa9; tests crates/ordo-cli/tests/check_exit.rs a_blind_index_lookup_that_returns_the_sealed_field_compiles, crates/ordo-host/tests/sealed_reads.rs a_declared_blind_index_lookup_applies_and_returns_the_opened_value

name: Totals and groups over a sealed field are refused, though documented as allowed
sub: Host-side folds after go-live (owner ok 2026-10-09)
explain:
Totals over a sealed value (sum, min, avg) are refused; count works.

  • Postgres holds only ciphertext, so SQL cannot add the values up.
  • The refusal now says what works instead, and the docs match (1ee4b03f).
  • Ordo could open each value on the server and fold there, at a cost per row.

asks.text: Should sum, min and avg over a sealed field be built, with Ordo opening each value on the server and adding them up there?
asks.suggest: Later, after go-live. It is correct but costs a decrypt per row; nothing waiting on it today, and the error already says what to do.

where: Refusal and docs corrected 1ee4b03f; test an_aggregate_over_a_sealed_value_is_refused_and_says_what_works_instead (ordo-sema)

name: Docs that promise what the code does not do
sub: Findings 4, 6 to 12, 14 to 19 fixed; 12 syntax-examples blocks marked planned
explain: Audit findings 4, 6 to 19: the README pitch uses route and a generated UI that do not exist, and its status says nothing runs; about 12 blocks in syntax-examples.md fail ordo check (CI only parses them); stale examples READMEs; 23 settings without rows; ordo help omits commands the guides use; the SDK README omits sign-in.
where: commits b3a6f88e, 378382f8; CI runs ordo check on every syntax-examples block: crates/ordo-cli/tests/syntax_examples_check.rs. Every ORDO_* the code reads has a docs/settings.md row (checked in docs/audit-2026-10-11.md, finding 14).

name: Build the medical billing example
decided: Just on the list is fine. It will be built later.
explain: The medical billing idea is on examples/IDEAS.md. Everything but sending claims and reading remittances (backend functions) works today.

asks.text: Build it now as a working example with synthesized data, marking the clearinghouse parts as planned?
asks.suggest: Yes, after the loading fixes. It exercises sealed fields, acl, roles, reports and delegation together, and a real app finds real bugs.

name: Refusals that do not name the setting to change
explain: Owner ruling 2026-10-08: a refusal a setting can fix names that setting and the value. Audit findings 30 to 34 list the ones that do not: a revert refusal naming a setting that does not exist, runtime refusals naming a capability, mail send refusals, boot refusals without a value, the OAuth2 return URL.
where: commit 4285b262: audit findings 30 to 34 (revert, six runtime refusals, mail send hints, boot numbers and master key, OAuth2 return URL); settings.md rows spelled out. Tests in revert_past_rescale, credential_reset, api, quotas, sharing, share_links, runtime, mail lib

name: Audit 2026-10-09: the small items still owed
explain:
Small audit items still owed (findings 13, 17, 20, 28).

  • Six fixed values become settings, today's value as the default.
  • ORDO_EGRESS_PRIVATE_HOSTS is read only when mail is on, so a bad value boots silently.
  • RevertPolicy has no setting outside Rust; 3 settings rows unidentified.

asks.text: ORDO_EGRESS_PRIVATE_HOSTS lets mail reach named private hosts. Should it apply to every outbound call (OIDC, Discord, Turnstile), and always be checked at boot?
asks.suggest: Yes, both. An in-cluster Keycloak needs it for OIDC, and a typo should stop the boot whether or not mail is on.

asks.text: It also accepts an exact IP such as 10.0.0.5, though the docs say host names only. Allow exact IPs?
asks.suggest: Yes, exact IPs only. Naming one address is as explicit as a name; ranges, wildcards and cloud metadata stay refused.

where: commit a17d3534: ORDO_EGRESS_PRIVATE_HOSTS parsed once at boot (DenyList::from_vars) for all egress, names, IPs and CIDRs, metadata always refused; 7 new settings (provider handoff, provider request, human check verify, recovery ticket, recovery codes per set, mail subject and text sizes); RevertPolicy documented as no setting yet; settings.md rows

name: Audit 2026-10-11: 30 findings, none High
explain:
The Fable batch audit of everything since 8cb5ccd6. 30 findings, 0 High. docs/audit-2026-10-11.md.

  • An op can be probed without a token (400 vs 403)
  • Public reads have no bound: each new parameter is a database read
  • Delegation requests are unauthenticated and unbounded
  • A stray … crashes the parser; 2 client calls can still hang

asks.text: Fix all 30 now, before public path phase 2?
asks.suggest: Yes, all 30. None is High, but 4 are reachable by any visitor of a public site, and phase 2 opens that door wider.

where: All 30 fixed 2026-10-11; each finding's commit and tests in docs/audit-2026-10-11.md. New settings: ORDO_PUBLIC_MISSES_PER_MINUTE, ORDO_DELEGATION_OPEN_PER_AGENT/_PER_PERSON, ORDO_AUTH_METHODS_MAX_AGE, ORDO_PUBLIC_CDN_PURGE_TIMEOUT_SECS, ORDO_AUTH_OIDC_STALE_GRACE_SECS, ORDO_AUTH_TENANT_LOCK_WAIT_MS, ORDO_AUTH_OIDC_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS, ORDO_AUTH_OIDC_ALGS.

name: The human check does not cover passkey sign-up
explain: Seen (audit finding 3): ORDO_AUTH_HUMAN_CHECK runs on /auth/begin only; /auth/register, the first leg of registerPasskey, never asks for a token, and the SDK's register options have no human field. Regression: a script creates passkey identities in bulk with the check on.

name: Limit an op the program writes to certain roles
sub: Defaults per op, tenant profiles, groups, no manager self-escalation
explain: Seen 2026-10-10 by the teamspace example: the door lets every role call authored reads, and editors and above call authored writes. Nothing lets the program say "this report is for admins only", so the report checks the role in its own body.

asks.text: Add a way to limit an op to roles in the program, e.g. op reportByProject for owner, manager = ...?
asks.suggest: Yes. The rule sits next to the op, the door refuses others before anything runs, and the client types know who may call it.

asks.text: The spec rules who-may-call-what is runtime, not syntax. So: the app developer ships a default per op, and each tenant owner may change it for their tenant. OK?
asks.suggest: Yes. The app gives sane defaults, a tenant fits them to its team, and nothing is baked into the program text.

asks.text: Tenants may only use the four roles today (owner, manager, editor, viewer). Should a tenant be able to define its own roles too?
asks.suggest: Later, after go-live. Per-op rules over the four roles cover the examples; custom roles touch every guard and acl and need their own design.

asks.text: The spec keeps roles at four, and gives tenants groups (named sets of members) with their own op lists instead. Is that what you meant by tenants' own roles?
asks.suggest: Yes, groups. A tenant makes "Finance" or "Support" as a group and grants it ops; no guard or acl has to learn a new role.

asks.text: A manager can change the tenant's profile. May a manager grant themselves (or their role) an op they do not already have?
asks.suggest: No. A manager may only hand out ops they can call themselves; only the owner may widen past that. Otherwise any manager can become owner-in-all-but-name.

name: A full database answers writes as access denied
explain:
Seen: at about 60 tenants on one door with default pool sizes, writes were refused as access_denied when Postgres ran out of connections.

Cause: the stale-grace fix (8959c7f7) covered part of it. Still denials: "too many connections" (53300) counted as a lasting fault, so the last good list was dropped; a failed read with no good list yet (new tenant, fresh boot); an unreadable share or delegation lookup.

Fix (77e6e3de): 53300 and 57P03 count as busy and keep the last good list; any space the door could not read answers 503 server_busy; so does an unreadable share or delegation lookup.

A regression looks like: a 403 while the database is full.

Guards: 3 tests in crates/ordo-host/tests/door_behind.rs, each failing with 403 before the fix. Authorization matrix green.

name: An email could be sent twice when a send lease ran out
explain:
CI caught one email sent twice. The bug is fixed. What remains is a gap no sender can fully close.

  • Ordo hands an email to the mail relay, then records "sent"
  • A crash between those two steps leaves Ordo not knowing whether it went
  • It must pick: send again (maybe twice) or never (maybe lost)
  • My earlier "every mail system" overstated it: this is true of any sender that records the hand-off separately, which is all SMTP senders

asks.text: If a crash lands between the relay accepting an email and Ordo recording it, should Ordo resend (maybe a duplicate) or not (maybe lost)?
asks.suggest: Resend, with the same Message-ID each time. A lost reminder is worse than a rare duplicate, and many mail clients fold two copies with one Message-ID into one.

where: mail.rs: lease fix (26acaaf5) and one Message-ID per email across resends; tests mail_outbox.rs

name: Notes v1 would not start on data from an earlier run
sub: Fixed 2026-10-22: ordo apply makes safe changes itself
explain:
The owner's first v1 run stopped at once (2026-10-21).

  • His local data predates the tags field
  • ordo apply refused: a new required field with a default needs ordo migrate --apply first
  • serve.sh then shut the door down
  • Fixed in serve.sh: it migrates, then applies again

Seen: schema behind, A3 new required field notes.tags with the constant default "[]", then REFUSED not activated, then shutdown.

Cause: the load gate refuses a program whose schema the database lacks, even for class A changes. serve.sh exits when ordo apply fails, and its trap stops the door.

Fix: examples/notes/dev/serve.sh runs ordo migrate --apply --db notes, then ordo apply again, when the first apply fails. Tried on a copy of the owner's data: the column was added, v1 activated, and 1 tenant database caught up.

Regression: serve.sh on data from an older notes.ordo stops instead of serving.

Tests: none automatic yet. The e2e stack starts from an empty database each run.

asks.text: Should ordo apply make safe additive changes itself (a new field with a default, a new index), and refuse only changes that can lose or reject data?
asks.suggest: Yes, as a setting, on by default. Adding a column with a default loses nothing, and a second command is a step every app developer will trip on. Data-risk changes stay refusals.

asks.text: Should the refusal print the exact ordo migrate command with this deployment's database filled in, instead of --db …?
asks.suggest: Yes. The host knows the database. A refusal the app developer can paste is the rule that a refusal names its fix.

where: schema_apply.rs apply_safe, ORDO_APPLY_SAFE_CHANGES (on), refusal names the real --db; tests ordo-cli schema_apply.rs, wire_apply.rs, ordo-host deploy_apply.rs; CI 39744627147 green

Fix: crates/ordo-api/src/sync.rs repeats check_access on every pass and ends the feed with the refusal; share_ops.rs close() signals after the seat is suspended. Commit 27bfb71a. Also found: notes-v2's unit tests were not in CI's examples list; added.

name: A tenant's pool could fill while a walker waited to dial
explain:
Found chasing a test that failed 3 ways on CI (2026-10-22). Fixed.

  • A walker took a slot in a tenant's pool, then waited on the node-wide dial cap with no time limit
  • Meanwhile requests to that tenant were refused as Saturated
  • Likely whenever a boot pass, a deploy catch-up and a sweep run at once

Fix: crates/ordo-exec/src/lib.rs Pool::acquire waits on the dial gate first and returns it once dialled. Commit e4beb853. Regression: requests to a tenant refused Saturated while walks run. Guarded by a_walker_waiting_on_the_dial_gate_holds_no_pool_slot (fails before, passes after) and route_many_tenants (30 of 30 under CPU load and against a password Postgres). The test's earlier slack was re-explained: 3 live walkers plus 2 backends still exiting.

asks.text: Should a wait for the dial cap have a time limit too, as a setting, so a stuck dial cannot hold walkers forever?
asks.suggest: Yes, generous by default (e.g. 60 s). The fix stops it blocking requests, but a walk stuck behind a dead cluster should end and say so.

where: e4beb853 Pool::acquire; 59fcc69f ORDO_PG_TENANT_DIAL_WAIT_MS; CI green on 3f014eaa

name: Sign-in answered 'store unavailable' when the server was only busy
explain:
Seen in CI (run 39902842452): an emailed-code begin answered 503 credential_store_unavailable. Fixed in part 2026-10-23.

  • Ops already answered a full pool as a retryable server_busy; sign-in did not
  • Two helpers stripped the pool's message before it reached the routes
  • Now the main sign-in paths and the mail outbox answer server_busy with Retry-After

Fix: passkeys.rs scrub and credentials.rs store_error keep a saturated cause; auth.rs store_failed / store_failed_for answer ApiError::server_busy; email_code.rs files a saturated enqueue as mail-outbox-busy; SDK PasskeyEndpoint.busyRetry retries server_busy in auth call(). Commit d3ae6558. Regression: a full pool on a sign-in route answers credential_store_unavailable. Guarded by crates/ordo-host/tests/auth_busy.rs (pool of 1 held: server_busy and Retry-After; dropped table: credential_store_unavailable) and clients/ordo-sdk/test/email.test.ts. Not yet covered: ~50 sites with no error in hand or an error already mapped (Failure::Unavailable, CompleteError::Unavailable), and auth SDK files that call fetch directly.

asks.text: Should the remaining ~50 sign-in spots, and the SDK's other sign-in calls, also tell "busy" apart from "broken" and retry busy?
asks.suggest: Yes, in one pass. Each spot today maps the error to a fixed word before the route sees it; carrying the cause through is mechanical. Same retry everywhere.

where: PoolError::is_busy; ordo_identity::StoreFault; auth/store_failure.rs; SDK auth/request.ts; commits 87f8309e, 51f7afb0; tests auth_busy.rs, auth_store_failure_scan.rs, auth-request.test.ts. Still text-typed elsewhere: in the service audit

name: CI test job evicted: runner docker-lib volume over 20Gi
explain:
The test job dies near its end, 4 runs in a row, as "runner lost communication". Every test step had passed.

  • Cause: the pod is evicted when its docker-lib volume passes 20Gi.
  • docker-lib holds the Postgres service, which keeps every test database.
  • The limit is in smg_infrastructure, so changing it needs your go.

Seen: CI on 17448906, fda32be1, 4e1bdf10 and 46909284 (2026-10-24), each about 35 minutes in. Event: Evicted pod/ordo-pool-2d8gs-runner-s7ffn: Usage of EmptyDir volume "docker-lib" exceeds the limit "20Gi". The pods have two 20Gi volumes, work (the cargo build) and docker-lib (dind: service containers and their data). The console crates added tests and databases, which tipped it over. Regression: a red CI with every test step green and the runner-lost annotation.

asks.text: May I raise the ordo-pool runner's docker-lib volume from 20Gi to 40Gi in smg_infrastructure?
asks.suggest: Yes. It is one line in the gha-runner values, and the node has room to check first. I will also add a CI step that prints Postgres's size so the next limit is chosen from a number.

name: Emailed codes claimed by the outbox but not sent for 20 s
explain:
Found by the store pool stress test (2026-10-24): emailed codes arrived about 2 minutes late.
- Cause: the outbox claim's `IN (SELECT ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)` reran per row under a nested-loop plan, so one claim leased several rows and sent one. The rest waited out the 120 s lease.
- Fix: the row is chosen in a `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`mail::claim_sql`). The job queue, trigger runs and attestation deliveries got the same shape.
- Commit 3d42f627. Tests force the nested-loop plan: `mail_outbox` `a_claim_leases_one_row_whatever_the_plan`, `jobs` `a_claim_of_n_takes_at_most_n_whatever_the_plan`.
Regression looks like: email begin answers 200, the code arrives about 2 minutes late, outbox rows with `attempts` 1 and `next_at` about 120 s out. The stress test reports `no_mail>0` with a STALLED dump.

- Fix 1: one helper (`ordo_api::blob::stored_bytes`) serves every stored byte with `sandbox; default-src 'none'` and `nosniff`. Only the default list renders inline; the rest download as `application/octet-stream`.
- Fix 2: cookie renewal needs an `Origin` on `ORDO_CORS_ORIGINS`.
Regression looks like: an HTML or SVG file served inline or with its claimed type, a blob or download response without the CSP, or `/auth/refresh` renewing from an unlisted origin. Guards: `stored_bytes_scan`, `auth_door` origin test.

- Cause: long-lived reads re-checked access only, never the token gate.

explain:
Found by CI on 782a8b86 (2026-10-25): a reader's shared note vanished after a second share was accepted, and came back only on reload.
- Cause: accepting replaces the share grant; since the feed check (0a016839) the reader's window token naming the old grant is refused, and the SDK treated that as revocation and erased the rows.

explain:
Seen (2026-10-31): CI's two-server reminder test timed out in 2 of 3 rounds. The second server's routine runs failed with "no key custody for space".

explain:
Seen (2026-10-31, CI authz matrix): a call sent once answered 409 idempotency_in_flight. Postgres had crashed and restarted moments before.

Cause: PgReplayCache::claim in crates/ordo-host/src/replay.rs read any failed statement as another request holding the key.

Fix: a database fault is ReplayClaim::Unavailable. After the same 5 s of retries the door answers 503 with Retry-After: server_busy for a full or starting database, else space_unavailable. Nothing runs.

A regression looks like: idempotency_in_flight while the database is down.

Guarded by: a_claim_on_a_database_that_is_gone_is_unavailable_not_in_flight (replay_durable.rs) and an_unreachable_replay_cache_is_not_an_identical_request_in_flight (ordo-api tests/api.rs).

group: Answered: your rulings, and what each one settled

name: Who the deployment owner is, and how they sign in
sub: Ruled 2026-10-01: separate sign-in through the backend. Today's model is documented
decided: yes
explain:
You noticed the deployment owner is not really a user of the app. Today Ordo treats them as one.

  • ORDO_DEPLOYMENT_OWNERS names a person who signed up through the app.
  • That makes them owner of the deployment's own tenant, where applying a program and creating tenants happen.
  • No doc explains this; the glossary has no entry.

How it works today

  • The deployment owner runs the server and holds its keys and database.
  • To act over the door (apply a program, create a tenant), a request needs a signed-in person who owns the deployment's own tenant.
  • The only way to be signed in is the app's own sign-in, so the owner signs up like a user and is then named in a setting.
  • On the command line with database access, the owner needs no sign-in at all.

Why it matters: the notes app's users and the deployment's owner share one sign-in and one list of people.

asks.text: Should the deployment owner sign in separately from the app's users?
asks.suggest: Yes, separately, through the console. The owner is not a customer of the app. Their sign-in belongs to the console (18o), with its own passkeys and its own list of people. Until the console exists, keep today's setting.

asks.text: Until then, should I write the glossary entry and a section in the deploying guide describing today's model?
asks.suggest: Yes. It is one page, and it stops the next person asking the same question.

where: Refined 2026-10-27: deployment people in the deployment space, separate credentials, admin role, no claim code, audited door acts; open asks on deployment-people-sign-in-machines-cli-and

name: Deleting a note that has an access row
sub: Ruled 2026-10-01: owned rows go with the note; who may delete them is a setting, default only the note
decided: OKay (the recommendation: the app developer's setting, default: only the note). Comment: A reminder that the app is just an example - but I understand it is teaching us things.
explain:
A note cannot be deleted today. Every note has an access row saying who owns it, and the delete counts that row as something still pointing at the note.

  • The spec says two different things about this. One ask settles it.
  • The notes app works around it by emptying a note instead of deleting it.

What the spec says (docs/definition-language.md)

  • About line 859: "owned cascades (part-of), association restricts (refuse-with-referrers)."
  • About lines 842 to 843: a link entity "dies with either end". The access table is one.
  • About line 2325, write rule 6: "tree/owned subtrees require the explicit subtree form."
  • subtree is only built for tree-shaped entities, and a note is not one.

Using subtree on a note is now a compile error rather than a failure at run time.

asks.text: When a note is deleted, should rows it owns, including its access rows, be deleted with it automatically?
asks.suggest: Yes, automatically. "Owned" means part of the note, and the spec's first rule says owned rows go with their owner. Rule 6's explicit form then stays for trees, where a delete can remove a large subtree.

asks.text: Deleting a note also deletes its access rows. Must the person be allowed to delete those rows too, or only the note?
asks.suggest: Make it the app developer's setting, default: only the note. Built today, only a note's admin can delete it, so someone you gave write access cannot. Access rows are Ordo's own bookkeeping, and most apps would expect write to be enough.

where: Cascade built: crates/ordo-conformance/src/write.rs. Revert of a create with owned rows built 2026-10-04: crates/ordo-exec/src/undo.rs, commit 2964fad, tests crates/ordo-exec/tests/owned_delete_revert.rs. Owed: 27m (the delete-permission setting, default: permission on the owner is enough) on both paths.

name: Live updates and the device copy in the React hooks: four choices
decided: 1 per entity seems like it would be pricey among tons of clients. Would it not make sense to keep 1 per client and share it? I'll take reccomendation either way
explain:
Read hooks can now update themselves when the server's data changes, and answer from the copy on the device. Both are off until an app turns them on.

  • The spec left four choices open. The builder made each; the asks let you keep or change them.

Details: clients/ordo-react/README.md, "Live and the device copy".

The device copy covers only reads that return identifiable rows. Counts, grouped results and the permission map always go to the network, and offline writes are refused, not queued.

asks.text: Should every read hook open a ?live=1 stream by default, so it updates when the data changes?
asks.suggest: Off by default; the app developer turns it on per hook or per provider. Yes, live means the ?live=1 stream on the read's own endpoint. Each one holds a server connection open.

asks.text: How often may a hook refetch when changes arrive quickly?
asks.suggest: Group bursts, and wait at least a quarter second between refetches, as a setting the app developer can change.

asks.text: Two lists on one page can update a moment apart. Build a coordinator so a page updates all at once?
asks.suggest: Later. It needs a position on every read the server does not send yet. File it for after the first deployment.

asks.text: Rows from the device come back in id order, not the read's own order. Fix that?
asks.suggest: Yes: the server should say each read's sort order in the interface, so the device can match it. Small, and wrong order is visible to people.

where: clients/ordo-react (hooks, live.ts, device.ts), crates/ordo-api/src/live.rs. 27o commit 9d1c40c; 27n commit 6c10ed4; 27s commits d27c9a5, 8379764. Coordinator: future task live-coordinator.

name: Evolution plans: render a schema change, keep it, apply it when ready, undo it
sub: Asks 1, 2, 4, 5 ruled 2026-10-01. Ask 3 put again with its cost: it would replace D-B2's one-version bound
decided: Stripe's makes the most sense (dual write through a soak; revert switches back to the previous shape, which stayed current). A step with no exact reverse is a different kind of error: "accept this one way change - revert requires this or manual intervention".
explain:
Today the migration is made fresh at each apply and nobody sees it first. The new spec keeps it.

  • How it works today, and why one version back: plan-evolution-plans.md section 1
  • A stored plan holds forward and reverse SQL per step
  • Each change offers options instead of a refusal
  • Every statement gets a lock timeout

The full proposal, with the option table per change type and the reverse rules, is docs/plan-evolution-plans.md. It extends plan-schema-evolution.md and keeps its A/B/C/D classes.

Ask 3, what serving many versions costs, against your example of 30 tenants on scattered versions among 400,000.

Small, and grows with the count:

  • Each node keeps one loaded program per served version and runs the shape gate per version. Kilobytes to a few megabytes each.
  • Clients need the interface for their tenant's version, so it is served per version.
  • A fix to the app's own ops reaches a tenant only when it moves. That is the app developer's call, as you said.

The real costs, paid once any old version is served:

  • Ordo's own releases. Every new Ordo binary must still load every artifact still served. The artifact format becomes a long-term promise, with tests per format.
  • Sharing between tenants. Feeds, windows and see-through read across spaces. If two tenants' versions differ on the shared entity, the read needs a rule: refuse, or translate.

What I would build: the app developer lists which versions stay served (a setting, default every version a tenant is on). Ordo serves any version its binary can load, and refuses sharing between tenants whose versions disagree on the shared entity until a translation exists. Custom builds for special tenants then use the same mechanism, filed for after first deployment as tenant-builds.

This replaces D-B2's one-back bound, so it is put to you as a ruling rather than assumed.

asks.text: Should ordo plan render and store the migration, and ordo apply run a stored plan when you are ready?
asks.suggest: Yes. It is your render-then-apply idea, and the same stored plan can then run in dev, staging and production unchanged.

asks.text: Keep every artifact and plan from one version before the oldest tenant's version onward?
asks.suggest: Yes. Keeping is cheap and already happens for artifacts. A tenant on 6 then replays 6 to 7 to 8, step by step, as D-B2 requires.

asks.text: Should the app developer decide which versions stay served, replacing D-B2's one-version-back bound?
asks.suggest: Yes. For 30 of 400,000 tenants the harm is small. The real costs come once any old version is served, whatever the count: every Ordo release must still load old artifacts, and sharing between tenants on different versions needs a rule.

asks.text: When a tenant fails to move to the new version, should it stay open on the old one while the deployment owner is told?
asks.suggest: Yes, while the old version is still served. Today it is held closed and retried every 15 seconds, which shuts its people out.

asks.text: Should choices like rename versus drop-and-add, or how to fill nulls, be made in the plan and never in the .ordo source?
asks.suggest: In the plan. The .ordo stays pure state. The choice is about getting from one state to the next, so it belongs to the step.

where: Spec: docs/plan-evolution-plans.md. Ruled: 27a (stored plans, receipt), 27b (keep everything), 27c (seamless). Ask 3 open: which versions stay served. Lock timeout: apply-lock-timeout (27d).

name: Changes a plan cannot generate forward, and how each is handled
sub: 21 asks ruled; 23 deferred to the syntax design. Ask 3 put again with an example
explain:
Some schema changes need a decision the old data cannot supply. Each ask is one case and how the plan would handle it.

  • Group 1: the new values do not exist
  • Group 2: more than one reading is valid
  • Group 3: a mapping fails for some rows
  • Group 4: the diff cannot see the change

asks.text: Group 1. A new required field with no default: should the plan offer a constant, an expression, or refuse?
asks.suggest: Offer all three, refuse by default. Old rows hold no value, so only the app developer can supply one.

asks.text: Group 1. A new field that records history, like createdBy on old rows: what should old rows get?
asks.suggest: Null with a marker meaning unknown, or a value the developer names. The history was never captured, and inventing it would be false.

asks.text: Yes, a date that gets now(). If due: date = today is added, should old rows get the migration day, or a date the developer gives?
asks.suggest: The developer gives it, with the migration day offered as one option. For new rows = today is their creation day. For old rows the migration day is a different, later date, so it should be a choice.

asks.text: Group 1. Adding an acl to an existing entity: who owns or may access each existing row?
asks.suggest: The developer picks a rule: the creator from the command log, the tenant's admins, or nobody. The command log already knows who created each row, so the first is usually available.

asks.text: Group 1. An entity becomes a tree but has no parent ref: how are paths built for old rows?
asks.suggest: Refuse until a parent ref exists, then derive the path from it. There is nothing to compute a path from.

asks.text: Group 2. A rename looks like a drop and an add: should a rename always be declared?
asks.suggest: Yes, declared in the plan; a drop-plus-add of the same type prompts the question. Guessing would copy one column into an unrelated one.

asks.text: Group 2. Moving a field to a related entity with several related rows: which row gets the value?
asks.suggest: The developer names the rule: first, latest, or copy to all. Refuse until named.

asks.text: Group 2. Splitting one entity into two, or merging two: how do old rows correspond to new ones?
asks.suggest: A declared correspondence rule, previewed on sample rows. Too many valid answers to guess.

asks.text: A link to many rows (a task's tags) becomes a link to one: when a row had several, which one stays?
asks.suggest: Refuse and list those rows, or a developer rule: first or latest. A ref is Ordo's link from one row to another, like author -> person. Dropped links go in the one-way warning.

asks.text: A text field (an author's name) becomes a link to a person row: what if a name matches no person, or several?
asks.suggest: List them and refuse until the developer fixes them, then link by their rule. A wrong link is worse than none.

asks.text: Owned links mean part-of (deleting a note deletes its comments); plain links only point. Should switching between them need a confirmation?
asks.suggest: Yes, a one-way style confirmation. No data moves, but what a delete does to existing rows changes, so the developer should agree to it.

asks.text: Group 3. Optional becomes required while nulls exist: how are nulls filled?
asks.suggest: A constant or expression, or refuse while nulls exist (the default). The probe already counts them.

asks.text: Group 3. Adding unique where duplicates exist: who chooses the surviving row?
asks.suggest: Always the developer, never automatic (your D7). The plan lists the duplicates and refuses until they are resolved.

asks.text: A required link is added (every task needs a project), but some old tasks have none or point at a deleted one. What then?
asks.suggest: Refuse, list those rows, and offer remediation: a project to assign, or an op to fix them. The same rule as nulls: pre-checks run on every tenant and report every issue at once.

asks.text: Group 3. Narrowing a type, like bigint to int or shorter text: what happens to values that do not fit?
asks.suggest: Refuse while any value does not fit, or a developer-named clamp or truncate. Silent truncation is data loss.

asks.text: Group 3. Text becomes an enum: what happens to values outside the set?
asks.suggest: Map each outside value to a member, or refuse. The probe lists every outside value.

asks.text: Group 3. Text becomes a date or number: how are mixed formats handled?
asks.suggest: The developer gives the formats; rows that parse none are listed and refused. Formats vary too much to guess.

asks.text: Group 3. Splitting one field into two, like full name into first and last: how is it parsed?
asks.suggest: A developer-given rule, with unparsed rows listed. Also a one-way step unless a join rule is given for the reverse.

asks.text: Emails are unique, and lowercasing is added. Ann@x.com and ann@x.com both exist and would become the same. What then?
asks.suggest: Refuse and list each collision; the developer merges or edits them first. Picking one silently would drop a person's row under a unique.

asks.text: Group 4. Same shape, new meaning, like cents becoming dollars: how does a plan learn of it?
asks.suggest: Let the developer attach a data rule to a step even when the schema did not change. No generator can see a change of meaning.

asks.text: Group 4. Values that should change because an outside system changed: does Ordo act?
asks.suggest: No; external entities report the foreign change, and the developer attaches a data rule if needed. Ordo only sees its own declaration.

asks.text: By design. Typed-id prefix change, unsealing, and several sealing steps in one deploy: keep refusing?
asks.suggest: Yes. Each is refused for a stated reason (D4, D6, D5): ids would stop being self-describing, or plaintext would leak permanently.

asks.text: Should prev (renames and correspondence) be written in the .ordo source, while fill values and rules stay in the plan?
asks.suggest: Yes. prev says what a thing is, which belongs with the declaration; fills say how to get there, which belongs to the step. Both are committed, so decisions stay on paper. Earlier you ruled choices in the plan; this narrows that.

asks.text: When old rows need a value for a text field, should the refusal suggest its 3 most used values (never sealed), as you proposed under filled?
asks.suggest: Yes, in dev and staging; in production only if the deployment owner turns it on. It shows tenant data in a plan's output, which a developer may not be allowed to see.

where: Ruled asks recorded in corpus-rulings. Ask 24 (suggest a text field's 3 most used values) waits for ordo evolve. Checklist 27a, 27w to 27z, 27an.

name: Public data on a web page: use cases, and the holes each finds
sub: Go 2026-10-09/10: build before the first deployment, read-only first
explain:
A visitor who is not signed in can read nothing today: the API refuses every request without a token. Each ask is one use case, the hole it finds, and what I would do.

  • Share links are the only way in, and they are secret
  • DL G15 says unguarded ops answer anonymous callers; the API disagrees

asks.text: Landing page shows the app's pricing and product catalogue. Should that live in the system space, read by anyone?
asks.suggest: Yes, the system space's read window, which a 2026-09-12 ruling promised and nothing built. Hole: the window does not exist yet.

asks.text: A person's public profile or blog. Should a tenant open chosen ops to anonymous visitors through a grant?
asks.suggest: Yes, a per-tenant anonymous grant, nothing public by default. Hole: no anonymous principal or grant exists, so G15 cannot be reached.

asks.text: A visitor opens example.com/ann. Every call must name its space id. How does a URL find the right tenant?
asks.suggest: A public slug per tenant, resolved by the door, that the tenant may set. Hole: the visitor never knows a space id, and none is guessable by design.

asks.text: A shop shows product photos to visitors. Should files on public rows be readable anonymously too?
asks.suggest: Yes, files follow their row's grant, as share links already do. Hole: /blob needs a token today, and public files want CDN caching.

asks.text: A row is half public: title shown, private notes hidden. How is part of a row made public?
asks.suggest: Expose an op that projects only the public fields. Guards work on rows, so the op's output is the boundary. Sealed fields must never appear in an anonymous op.

asks.text: A contact form or waitlist lets visitors write. Should anonymous writes be possible?
asks.suggest: Yes, per op as the developer's setting, off by default, with rate limits and a human check. Hole: G15 rejects every anonymous write today.

asks.text: Search across many shops (a marketplace). Where does that search run, with one database per tenant?
asks.suggest: A derived public index fed by each tenant's public rows. Hole: the index does not exist, and a live query across every tenant database would not scale.

asks.text: A public feed mixing posts from thousands of tenants. Build it the same way as search?
asks.suggest: Yes, the same derived index. Each tenant pushes its public rows out (a feed), which a 2026-09 ruling already found cheaper than reading across databases.

asks.text: Anonymous traffic can flood: bots, crawlers, scrapers. Should anonymous requests get their own limits?
asks.suggest: Yes, separate limits per tenant and per caller address, as settings. Hole: no anonymous rate limit exists, and one tenant's crawler must not slow others.

asks.text: Every anonymous read could write an audit row. Should anonymous reads be audited one by one?
asks.suggest: No: counted, not logged one by one; writes are always logged. Hole: the stream would grow without bound under crawler traffic.

asks.text: A public status page shows live counts. Should anonymous visitors get live updates?
asks.suggest: Yes, but through one shared stream per page, not per visitor. Each live stream holds a server connection, so thousands of visitors need sharing (your 27s idea).

asks.text: A post is unpublished or erased, but crawlers and CDNs cached it. What does Ordo promise?
asks.suggest: Ordo stops serving it at once and tells caches to drop it; copies already taken are out of reach. The erasure receipt should say so plainly.

asks.text: Developers want open data through a public API with keys. Is that anonymous access, or a credential?
asks.suggest: A credential: an API key is a capability token with an allowlist. Anonymous stays for browsers with no account; keys get per-key quotas.

asks.text: A page embedded on another site calls Ordo from that site. Should each tenant choose its allowed origins?
asks.suggest: Yes, per tenant as a setting. Hole: CORS origins are one list for the whole deployment today.

asks.text: Should public data live in the deployment's space, with tenants private and contributing only by submission or grant?
asks.suggest: Yes. It is the model your answers point to: a forum post is a submission, a marketplace listing is a grant to the deployment. The privacy wall stays.

asks.text: Add a public qualifier to entities and fields, with public* cascading to children, refused by the compiler on sealed fields?
asks.suggest: Yes. Public becomes declared and checked, so the Supabase failure, a table left open by a forgotten policy, cannot happen.

asks.text: Should a public op be allowed to write into a private entity, write-only, for contact forms and waitlists?
asks.suggest: Yes, as the developer's opt-in per op, with a rate limit. Nobody reads the rows back publicly, and the writes are logged like any other.

asks.text: Cache public op results, dropped exactly when an entity the op reads changes?
asks.suggest: Yes. Ordo already knows every entity an op reads. Others cache on a timer; Ordo can drop a cached answer the moment it goes stale.

asks.text: Serve public traffic from a dedicated read layer that scales out on its own, in front of the database?
asks.suggest: Yes. It serves cached public results and holds no database connection per visitor, so public load never reaches the database.

asks.text: Add a build-time credential that runs public ops while a static site builds, so data is baked into the pages?
asks.suggest: Yes, as an option. It is a capability token limited to public ops, so a leaked one exposes nothing that was not already public.

asks.text: For an app whose product is an API, should keys be issued to the app's customers, each naming its ops and quota?
asks.suggest: Yes. The customer is a principal or a tenant, the key is a revocable capability token, and CORS origins become a per-tenant setting.

asks.text: A forum post as a submission into the deployment's space breaks the 2026-09-12 rule that tenants' writing stays in their own space. Which wins?
asks.suggest: Keep posts in the author's space, shown through a feed and the derived index. Erasure and consent then follow the author. Submissions stay for app-owned content.

asks.text: Tenants read the deployment's space at three levels: public, any signed-in person by default, or narrowed by a developer's guard. Is that right?
asks.suggest: Yes. Ordo gives the default and the guard; the app developer decides who sees what. Plan §7a.

asks.text: Build the public path now, read-only first, so the marketing site example (and forum, blog, status page) can be real? It blocks 7 example ideas.
asks.suggest: Yes, read-only first. Public reads unblock the marketing site; public writes (contact forms) can follow as a second step.

asks.text: Public writes (contact forms): with no per-address limit (IPs are out), bound them by a per-op hourly cap and require the human check by default?
asks.suggest: Yes, both, as settings. The cap stops a flood without knowing who sent it; Turnstile stops scripts. An app can turn either off for its own reasons.

asks.text: Which public pieces before the first deployment: writes, per-tenant CORS, the read layer, live public pages, API keys, the forum index?
asks.suggest: Writes and per-tenant CORS before; the rest after. They cover forms and embeds; one server plus the cache and a CDN carry first traffic.

asks.text: Move the marketing site example from its share link to public ops as soon as writes land, and keep the share-link version as a second example?
asks.suggest: Move it, and drop the share-link version. Two ways to do one thing confuses a first reader; share links stay shown in notes.

asks.text: Normal systems slow one busy visitor by address. Behind a CDN all visitors share its address, so that needs proxy mode (post-deploy now). Bring it forward?
asks.suggest: Yes, slow-down only, off until proxy mode is set. An address only ever delays a visitor, never refuses; monitoring counts public requests either way.

asks.text: Public writes (a contact form) are capped per op per hour. Is 1000 per op per hour, per server, the right default?
asks.suggest: Yes, 1000. Room for a busy launch day, small enough that a script fills the hour fast and stops. 0 turns it off; the refusal names the setting.

asks.text: May tenants list their own allowed origins (embeds) only once the deployment owner allows it? Built off by default.
asks.suggest: Yes, off until allowed. A tenant's list widens who may call; the deployment owner turns it on with ORDO_CORS_TENANT_ORIGINS_MAX, named in the refusal.

asks.text: A newsletter sign-up with an email already taken: answer the same "thanks" as a new one, instead of refusing such forms?
asks.suggest: Yes, same answer either way. A refusal tells a visitor whose email is listed. Built now as refused; one answer for both lets the form exist and leaks nothing.

asks.text: Run the human check before counting a public write against the hourly cap, so junk never uses up the hour?
asks.suggest: Yes. Costs one Turnstile call per junk token, which Cloudflare absorbs; otherwise a script without tokens could block every real form for the hour.

asks.text: Should a tenant's own public site (a shop) take public writes into that tenant's space, not only the deployment's?
asks.suggest: Yes, next. Shopfront and per-tenant forms need it. The program's public grant names the ops; the space comes from the site's address. Not built yet.

where: Phase 1 built 2026-10-10 (706020ab, 5c6f2fa4, bb615bac, f94fdac8). Phase 2 built 2026-10-11 (4a43e096 writes, 4ea02e5a per-tenant CORS, 597bfc7a proxy mode, e15aa270 marketing site, 22741376 docs, 5c074752 layered human check); asks 29 to 32 applied 2026-10-12 (19f7a744: cap 10000, keyed creates answer alike); tests ordo-host public_writes.rs, ordo-api cors_layers.rs, ordo-plan public_ops.rs, marketing_site_app.rs. Later: read layer, live public, API keys, derived index, [[public-writes-tenant-space]].

name: Public writes into a tenant's own space
explain: Owner, 2026-10-12 (public-data ask 33): a shop's public writes go to the deployment; a write that stays inside one tenant's boundary is a niche case. Filed for after the first deployment.
